Date: 2026-03-10
Start: 09:32 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Avery Stone (Redwood SE); Mark Jensen (CTO, Lakeside), Sara Lopez (Head of ML), Ryan Murphy (Infra Lead), Emily Cho (Security)

summary: Discovery focused on Lakeside Bank's needs for dedicated GPU capacity. Discussed isolation requirements, burst/burstback strategy, expected QPS and token distributions, VPC and KMS needs, SOC2/compliance, and benchmarking expectations. Agreed to run a short benchmark and share pricing + runbook. Customer leaning towards Dedicated for data isolation but wants clear cost/latency tradeoffs vs Hosted.
topics: Current inference stack and pain points
Security: SOC2, KMS, audit logs, SSO/SAML
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everybody, thanks for taking the time. Quick intros, then we'll jump into what you run today and what you're trying to achieve with dedicated capacity.
[00:12] Mark (Lakeside CTO): Sure, I'm Mark, CTO. We've got Sara leading models, Ryan infra, Emily on security. We're looking to move some models off the public hosted endpoints because of data residency and isolation.
[00:25] Jordan: Got it. Priya is our Solutions Engineer, she'll dig into workloads and perf. Priya?
[00:30] Priya (Redwood SE): Hey all, nice to meet you. Can you give a sense of current traffic - QPS, average tokens, peak patterns?
[00:38] Sara: Right now prod is about 6 QPS average, peaks up to ~90 QPS during business hours for some flows, average tokens per request is 220 but we have long-form workflows that go to 1,500 tokens occasionally.
[00:52] Ryan: We're seeing p95 generation latencies around 1.1s on Hosted for short prompts but tail and long sequences are heavier. Cost is ramping up too.
[01:05] Priya: Thanks. That profile actually maps well to a Dedicated pool scenario where you can reserve GPU capacity to hit predictable p95s and control burst behavior. For bursts, you can configure burst pools or autoscale - Jordan will cover pricing differences.
[01:20] Jordan: Right. Just to set expectations, Dedicated is reserved capacity - you get isolation and predictable throughput. You can configure burst capacity for short spikes, but sustained bursts require additional commit or higher plan.
[01:33] Mark: Can you explain the isolation - VPC vs on-prem? We need to know what traffic and secrets stay in our VPC.
[01:40] Avery (Redwood SE): Sure. With Redwood Dedicated we offer a VPC peering option where inference nodes live in a customer VPC or a private subnet within our infra depending on region. For highly regulated cases we also support our Private product that self-hosts the control plane and inference nodes on-prem. There can be some differences in telemetry and management between options.
[01:55] Emily (Security): For Dedicated, do you support KMS/HSM integration and customer-managed keys? Also audit logs and retention policies?
[02:04] Priya: Yes, KMS integration is supported for Dedicated and Private. Audit logs are available, retention configurable as an add-on. We have SOC2 documentation and can share encryption-in-transit and at-rest details.
[02:15] Emily: We'll need SSO/SAML with SCIM and RBAC for roles.
[02:18] Jordan: We support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning and role-based access controls. We'll share the security pack after the call.
[02:27] Sara: On the modeling side, we care about quantization and perf. Which GPUs do you recommend? We have seq len variability, lots of KV cache usage.
[02:36] Priya: For mixed seq lengths we generally recommend A10G or A100-based pools depending on model size and latency targets. We can surface recommended kernel/quantization profile in our Optimize recommendations. For KV cache heavy workloads, the runtime handles KV eviction and caching - we'll want to run a benchmark to tune batch sizes and cache parameters.
[02:52] Ryan: Is the runtime yours or do we host Triton? We have internal infra that uses Triton and HF endpoints.
[02:58] Avery: It's our GPU-optimized inference runtime. We do expose standard APIs so migration is straightforward, but we keep optimizations like continuous batching and KV cache management under the hood. Some customers also run Triton on-prem, but then you'd be looking more at Redwood Private or self-hosted solutions.
[03:12] Mark: Pricing - baseline committed capacity monthly plus overage or burst credits? How does that work in practice?
[03:19] Jordan: Typically there's a monthly reserved capacity commit, with an option to configure a burst pool that draws on short-term burst credits. Overage beyond committed baseline is billed at higher unit price; we can model a hybrid approach if you expect very spiky traffic.
[03:32] Ryan: For spikes we need sub-second cold-starts and consistent p50/p95. How do you handle cold model loading?
[03:39] Priya: Cold starts for large models can be 10s if loading from scratch; we keep warm workers and prefetch for common model variants. Dedicated pools let you keep persistent workers so cold starts are rare. For very bursty patterns you can configure a small warm standby pool.
[03:55] Sara: We are also evaluating Hosted with VPC peering vs Dedicated - what's the expected unit cost diff?
[04:02] Jordan: Hosted is generally cheaper at low volume, Dedicated gives predictable unit economics at scale. We'll send a cost comparison with your usage profile factored in.
[04:12] Mark: On compliance - we need SOC2 Type II, encryption with CMK, and data residency within US-East.
[04:20] Emily: Also, retention of request logs should be 90 days and must be deletable on demand.
[04:26] Priya: We can meet SOC2, CMK integration, and US-East region deployments. Audit log retention is configurable; we can add a deletion workflow. We'll include the documentation.
[04:36] Jordan: Quick qual: what's the timeline and success criteria?
[04:40] Mark: Timeline is end of Q2 for pilot (so ~June). Success criteria: p95 latency <800ms for our short prompts, cost per 1k tokens under target we shared, and SOC2 + KMS integration validated.
[04:52] Priya: Good. For the benchmark, we'll need sample prompts, expected QPS curve, and longest seq lengths. We'll run tests with quantized model variants and share results.
[04:59] Ryan: Network - we use strict egress rules. Will we need to open ports?
[05:03] Avery: For VPC peering, minimal egress needed; we'll document required firewall rules. For Private on-prem we'll run entirely inside your network.
[05:12] Sara: One concern - how seamless are rollouts and model version pinning? We need reproducible behavior across dev/staging/prod.
[05:19] Jordan: We support model pinning and can do canary rollouts, A/B, and automatic fallback to pinned variants. Console gives per-route dashboards.
[05:28] Mark: Any gotchas with large KV caches causing memory pressure on GPUs?
[05:33] Priya: That's why we tune cache sizes and eviction policies; we'll run a targeted stress test. For very large KV sizes we may recommend multi-node sharded KV or quantization to reduce per-token memory.
[05:44] Customer (Sara): Are there any limits on custom models? We want to bring our fine-tuned models.
[05:49] Priya: You can bring custom models; we do model onboarding and can test perf+compatibility. For some internal model formats we may need minor conversion.
[05:57] Jordan: Ok let's recap next steps - I'll send pricing and a tailored cost model; Priya will share the benchmark runbook; Ryan will share metrics; Emily will send security requirements. We'll schedule the benchmark kickoff for the week of 2026-03-22.
[06:12] Mark: Sounds good. Any other questions?
[06:15] Emily: One last - encryption at rest with customer keys, is key rotation supported?
[06:20] Priya: Yes, CMK rotation is supported, we can document the process.
[06:24] Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts.
[06:28] End of recording.

Notes about transcript quality: moderate auto-transcription errors in a few product names (e.g., 'Redwood Private' sometimes transcribed as 'Redwood privatee') and occasional speaker mis-attribution. Benchmark items and links mentioned are in the shared drive.
